title: Feeding the hungry
hook: the Prophet's first words in Medina: spread peace, feed people, pray at night
tomorrow: how do you help someone who's in the wrong?

segments.voice: Yesterday: the best of people are the ones most useful to people. Useful can sound huge. Today it starts with a plate.

A new boss's first meeting. A new coach's first talk in the locker room. Everyone listens hard, because first words tell you what someone cares about. Now a crowd at Medina, pushing to see a man who has just arrived: the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. In the crowd is a man named 'Abdullah ibn Salam, who came, he says, with everyone else, just to get a look. He gets close, studies the newcomer's face, and decides one thing: this is not the face of a liar. Then the Prophet speaks. What comes first?
screen: `FIRST WORDS SHOW WHAT MATTERS.` → `A CROWD AT MEDINA.` → `NOT THE FACE OF A LIAR.`

segments.voice: 'Abdullah ibn Salam tells it in Jami' at-Tirmidhi. The first thing he heard was a short list. O people: spread the greeting of peace, feed people, and pray at night while others sleep, and you will enter Paradise in peace. Look at that list. One greeting. One meal. One quiet prayer in the dark. Nothing on it needs a title or a budget. A greeting costs nothing. A meal costs a little. A prayer in the dark costs some sleep. And feeding sits right between a hello and a prayer, as if a plate and a prostration belong in the same breath. The Qur'an praises the same thing. In Pickthall's words, the righteous "feed with food the needy wretch, the orphan and the prisoner, for love of Him." The next verse gives what they say as they do it: we want no reward from you, and no thanks. That's the detail worth telling a friend tonight. In the Qur'an's picture, the one who feeds isn't even waiting for a thank-you. The meal is the whole point. So feeding the hungry is a food bank and a fundraiser, yes. It's also the extra plate when a friend drops by, the lunch split down the middle, the granola bar handed through a car window. Feed people.
screen: `SPREAD PEACE, FEED PEOPLE, PRAY AT NIGHT.` · `A PLATE BESIDE A PRAYER.` · `FOR LOVE OF HIM, NO THANKS WANTED.` · `THE EXTRA PLATE COUNTS.` · then, large: `FEED PEOPLE.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind one person you could feed this week: a roommate, a coworker, a neighbor, someone who always skips lunch. See the food in your hand and the moment you pass it over. Then name the one thing most likely to stop you, and one simple way around it.
screen: `ONE PERSON.` · `THE FOOD IN YOUR HAND.` · `WHAT STOPS YOU, AND THE WAY AROUND.`

segments.voice: Feeding the hungry: sharing food with someone who needs it. In 'Abdullah ibn Salam's report, it comes right after the greeting of peace.
Your line: feed people. A plate is enough to start, and nobody owes you thanks for it. See you tomorrow.

screen: `DAY 1737 COUNTS.` → `SERVICE AND JUSTICE · 2 OF 10.` → `TOMORROW: HOW DO YOU HELP SOMEONE IN THE WRONG?`

howItsDone: Muslims feed people in ordinary and organized ways: an extra plate for guests and neighbors, food shared at the mosque, meals given to the poor, and iftar hosted for those breaking the Ramadan fast.

myth: in the Qur'an, the people who feed the needy expect at least a thank-you
76:9 has them say it plainly: we want no reward from you, and no thanks.
'feed people' sits in the same short list as praying at night
spread peace, feed people, pray while others sleep: that's the report in Tirmidhi.
feeding the hungry only counts when it goes through a charity
charity counts, and so does the extra plate. the hadith just says: feed people.

fork.setup: your family has a big dinner tonight. your cousin's new coworker is in town alone and texts your cousin for restaurant tips. what does 'feed people' point to?
options: invite her to dinner; one more plate is the hadith in action.
send a good restaurant list; she asked for tips, not for a meal.
wait until you know her; feeding is for people who are close.
fork.reveal: the list was short: spread peace, feed people, pray at night. nothing about knowing them first, and in 76:8 the fed even include a prisoner.

original.note: Arabic: 'feed food', the Prophet's words in 'Abdullah ibn Salam's report.

trapdoor: what you thought: feeding the hungry is a job for charities and food banks.
what it means: among the first words 'Abdullah ibn Salam heard, 'feed people' sits between a greeting and a prayer: a plate anyone can give.
what a scholar hears: Tirmidhi's report, at'imu at-ta'am, 'feed food', with Qur'an 76:8-9: food given to the needy, the orphan and the prisoner for love of Him, with no thanks wanted.
guess: giving food to someone who needs it
fasting so you know what hunger is
a fund that buys meals for the poor

chat.says: girl on my floor has skipped dinner twice, says she's 'saving money'. i have extra meal swipes. weird to offer?
options: Not weird. Make it easy: 'come eat with me?' Feeding people sits right beside prayer.
Leave it. Offering food could embarrass her, so wait until she asks you first.
Give the swipes to the campus pantry; feeding the hungry means strangers, not friends.
chat.meaning: Among the first words 'Abdullah ibn Salam heard: feed people, beside greeting and prayer. The Qur'an praises feeding that wants no thanks back.

'Abdullah ibn Salam.meaning: a man of Medina who reported the Prophet's first words there

Medina.meaning: the city the Prophet moved to from Mecca

Jami' at-Tirmidhi.meaning: a major collection of the Prophet's sayings and deeds

Pickthall.meaning: a public-domain English translation of the Qur'an

notes: Confirm the exact Pickthall wording of 76:8 (the verse opens 'And feed with food...'; the quotation starts at 'feed').

Tirmidhi 2485: confirm numbering and the paraphrase. Some versions (Ibn Majah 1334) add 'keep the ties of kinship'; the script follows the outline's three items. 'The first thing he heard' follows the report's own framing.
